description: For an L2 learner who produces a form but distributes it unlike proficient users because the L1 divides the meaning differently, explaining the meaning that motivates the form's uses (its core sense, with diagrams) and then practising choices across contexts is expected to yield more appropriate use than structural or phrase-only teaching; no claim in the wiki tests this comparison.
title: Teach the conceptual underpinnings of L2 forms rather than only their structural aspects or formulaic units

description: For learners working toward understanding they can use, a teacher who states the goal, organizes a task learners act on, questions and helps contingently while they work, and has them explain and transfer what they understood is expected to yield more engagement and usable understanding than presenting the content, provided novices still get explicit guidance; no claim in the wiki tests the teacher's role directly, only neighbouring comparisons (active learning against lecture, teacher-led against student-led inquiry).
title: Educators should act as mediators and facilitators of learning rather than content disseminators

description: For a teacher who needs families' cooperation, relationship-first contact and regular two-way communication about learning, begun before any problem, are expected to build more teacher-parent trust and fewer escalations than relying on rules notices and remote sanctions; no claim tests that comparison, though partnership-programme trials and a home-visit study test parts of it.
title: Strengthen ties between teachers and parents rather than pressing for remote sanctions behind teaching

description: When a tool could do part of a task the learner must learn to do unaided, using it so the learner still does that part (attempt first; hints, questions and feedback rather than solutions; simulation or VR beside hands-on practice, not instead of it) is expected to give better performance once the tool is removed than letting it take the part over; single studies of generative AI with adults test this, three experiments limit it, and no claim tests complement against replacement for simulation or VR.
title: Technology should augment, not supplant, learning processes in student-centered environments

description: For learners who need practice writing for a live audience or a lower-threshold way to ask and respond, a focused text chat on a closed task, with content prepared beforehand and someone keeping the pace legible, is expected to produce negotiation of meaning, self-correction and wider participation, but no claim in the wiki tests chat against the same task without it on a learning outcome.
title: Text Chats

description: For a learner whose barrier to a text is decoding, vision or fatigue rather than its language, and when the goal is its meaning rather than reading the words, hearing the text read aloud while following the print with control of pace is expected to raise comprehension over print alone; no claim in the wiki tests text-to-speech itself.
title: Text-to-Speech
